summary:
ALTAIR (Autonomous Space-Earth Fidelity Engine) is an advanced telemetry-driven web application developed by team Stalred (STRD) to address the “Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars” challenge.

ALTAIR bridges planetary science and mission planning by combining hardheaded baseline parameters from NASA LRO Diviner and PDS datasets with real-time Earth telemetry queried via the NASA POWER API. Through an interactive tactical command center map and an automated similarity calculation engine, users can evaluate terrestrial environments against extreme space targets—factoring in specific mission hardware like rovers, habitats, and EVA suits—while instantly generating rigorous operational risk assessments.

This tool is vital because traditional analogue research is often slow and decentralized. ALTAIR provides mission architects, researchers, and space agencies with an immediate, data-backed fidelity validation engine, accelerating site selection, optimizing analog testing, and significantly reducing logistical and operational risks for future human colonization on the Moon and Mars.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

ALTAIR (Autonomous Space-Earth Fidelity Engine) is an advanced telemetry-driven web application designed to identify and validate terrestrial environments on Earth that serve as accurate analogues for permanent lunar base locations and Mars. The system operates via a dual architecture:

  1. Backend: Built using Python with FastAPI, it combines a hardcoded planetary reference dataset derived from NASA LRO Diviner Lunar Data and NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) baseline parameters (e.g., Shackleton Crater and Jezero Crater) with live Earth telemetry queries fetched dynamically via the public NASA POWER API. It features a fidelity calculation engine that computes a weighted similarity score (0–100%) by comparing live Earth coordinates against space targets while factoring in mission-specific hardware.
  2. Frontend: Developed using React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet, it presents a professional, utilitarian aerospace command center interface featuring interactive maps, toggleable NASA GIBS (Worldview) satellite tile layers, hardware selectors, and live risk-assessment telemetry panels.

What benefits and intended impact does it have?

Traditional planetary analogue research is often fragmented and slow. ALTAIR provides an immediate, data-backed validation tool that accelerates site selection, optimizes analogue testing for field researchers and space agencies, and rigorously evaluates operational risks (thermal, solar, barometric, and aridity constraints) to minimize mission hazards for future human exploration.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Languages & Frameworks: Python, FastAPI, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS.
  • Mapping & Libraries: Leaflet (React-Leaflet), Lucide React icons, HTTPX.
  • APIs & Data Sources: NASA POWER API, NASA GIBS / Worldview WMTS satellite layers, NASA LRO Diviner, and Planetary Data System (PDS) datasets.
  • Deployment & Tooling: Vercel (Frontend), Render (Backend), Git, and Porkbun DNS routing (altair.earth).

How is your project creative and what factors did the team consider?

ALTAIR breaks away from generic map templates by adopting a strict, high-density professional UI inspired by SpaceX telemetry dashboards and mission control terminals—avoiding cartoonish or artificial "AI-looking" designs. The team (Stalred / STRD) carefully balanced scientific validity with real-world utility, ensuring that every calculation reflects genuine planetary constraints (such as regolith composition, extreme temperature ranges, and atmospheric pressure) while maintaining seamless, lightning-fast execution suited for rapid hackathon deployment.
